newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israel's ambassador to Jordan resigns.
newsitem.headline: Israel's ambassador to Jordan resigns.

text.p: Israel's ambassador to Jordan has resigned after just one week at his post in protest at being kept in the dark about a meeting between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and King Hussein, diplomatic sources said on Tuesday.
They said the summit in Jordan last Thursday was "the latest in a chain of events", including plans for other high-level meetings, which ambassador Oded Eran had not been consulted on.
Israeli embassy officials confirmed Eran's resignation but declined to give a reason for it.
"(Israel's) Foreign Ministry Director General Eitan Ben Tzur confirmed that he received the resignation letter but hopes the ambassador will reconsider," embassy spokesman Shalom Tourgeman said.
He said Eran had left for Brussels on Monday night on a pre-arranged trip after hosting an embassy reception celebrating the anniversary of Israel's creation in 1948.

King Hussein met Netanyahu in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba on Thursday to resolve a dispute over water rights granted to Jordan under their 1994 peace treaty. The row caused the cancellation of a joint ceremony to commemorate seven Israeli girls shot dead by a Jordanian soldier in March.
Eran, formerly deputy director general for economic affairs at Israel's Foreign Ministry, was only Israel's second ambassador to Jordan since the two countries opened up embassies two years ago.
